title: Learning Manifold and Itô Dynamics with Branched Neural Rough Differential Equations
claim: A control path and a set of vector fields are each lifted into a shared algebraic basis, then combined into one local update.
layout: Sphere at left, zoom to two inputs, two-branch flow top-to-bottom into equation box
description: A large grey 3D sphere on the left carries a jagged blue sample path. A small pink square on the path is labeled T_Z M, and thin lines zoom it into a rounded box at top right. That box is split into two panels. The left panel, 'Vector Fields (W)', shows a field of blue arrowheads with a black curve and a dashed pink curve. The right panel, 'Driver (X_{s,t})', shows a noisy red path. Two arrows run downward from the panels. The left arrow, labeled F, ends at a row of colored rooted-tree icons with the label F_W(p). The right arrow ends at matching trees labeled Sig^N_H(X)_{s,t}. A 'Primitivize log_H' arrow leads from the right branch, and an arrow from the left branch, into a rounded 'Log-ODE Solve' box. That box holds the equation L_{s,t} = sum <p, λ_{s,t}> F_W(p). The eye goes first to the sphere and then to the colored trees.
caption: Illustration of the log-ODE method for \glspl{bnrde}. The control segment $X_{s,t}$ is lifted to $X^\mathcal{H}_{s,t} \in \mathcal{H}^{(\le N)}$ for the chosen Hopf algebra $\mathcal{H} \in \{\hopfshuf, \hopfgl, \hopfmkw\}$, then transformed to a log-signature $\lambda_{s,t}$ in primitive coordinates $p \in \mathcal{B}_\mathcal{H}^\mathrm{prim}$. The tangent vector fields $\mathcal{W}$ are lifted through the pseudo bialgebra map $F_{\mathcal{W}}$ to matching primitive-indexed vector fields on the state manifold. These are combined into the log-ODE vector field $L_{s,t}$, whose ODE flow gives the local update from $s$ to $t$.
abstract: Neural rough differential equations (NRDEs) stay accurate under irregular sampling while taking far fewer integration steps than standard neural differential equations, summarising a finely sampled driver by its log-signature and advancing the hidden state over coarse intervals using the log-ODE method. This efficiency rests on the shuffle algebra, the algebraic counterpart of Stratonovich calculus. This reliance means NRDEs cannot expose the quadratic-variation terms ItÃ´ dynamics require, nor the ordered covariant derivatives that govern ItÃ´ flows on connection-equipped manifolds. Ameliorating this, we introduce Branched Neural Rough Differential Equations (B-NRDEs), a Hopf-algebraic framework that recasts the NRDE log-ODE step as geometric numerical integration on the state-space manifold, matching the driving algebra to the governing calculus: Grossman--Larson rooted trees for Euclidean ItÃ´ dynamics, the Munthe--Kaas--Wright dual for ordered covariant derivatives on manifolds, and the tensor algebra in the classical Stratonovich case. This yields intrinsic coarse-step dynamics that exactly preserve manifold constraints. Finally, we introduce a branched signature-kernel objective to enable ItÃ´-consistent law matching by making quadratic variation terms visible during training. On rough Bergomi volatility, sim-to-real $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ forecasting, and SPD covariance dynamics, B-NRDEs offer a unified, effective approach to stochastic and manifold-valued dynamics beyond the Euclidean--Stratonovich setting.
